advices.diagnosis: The class has a very high number of methods (NOM 25) and a large sum of cyclomatic complexity (WMC 49), indicating a single class is handling many responsibilities. The cohesion metric LCOM4 is 4, far above the acceptable threshold, meaning the class is composed of several disconnected components. The class also references eight other internal classes (DCC 8), showing high coupling. The low DAM (1.0) shows almost no private attributes, which is typical for a god object. Together these metrics reveal a classic god‑object anti‑pattern: a single class that mixes order handling, pricing, logging, and notification logic.

suggestions.title: Split OrderManager into focused services

advices.risk_notes: The split will increase the number of classes in the codebase, which may raise the overall project DCC if not managed carefully. Additionally, if the original OrderManager was used as a singleton or injected via a framework, the new services must be wired correctly. Finally, the change may affect performance if the façade adds overhead; profiling should be performed after the refactor.
